blocks.name: Krua Jay Sim
blocks.descHtml:
Budget runs 251–500 THB per person, cash only. Sample dishes: moo khua chaew THB 150, tod man pla krai THB 200, kaeng pa with fish cakes THB 240; the stir-fried black pepper prawns and tom yum mackerel are priced by the day's market rate. There's no online booking system — call ahead at 08-1351-4569, or just walk in. On weekends, arrive before noon, since Bangkok day-trippers fill the place up for weekend lunch.

You can only get here by car — no train or public transit reaches it. From Bangkok it's about 45–60 minutes' drive, and the restaurant has its own car park. The key thing is pinning the right location — the restaurant has moved several times, and the current address is 98/17 Moo 2, Soi Khun Kaeo 12, Khun Kaeo subdistrict, Nakhon Chai Si. Don't use an old pin in town. Open Tuesday–Sunday 09:00–15:30, closed Mondays. It's a daytime-only restaurant, so plan it as a lunch stop on a Nakhon Chai Si trip rather than dinner. blocks.name: Nai Ngieb
blocks.descHtml:
Budget is easy on the wallet, around 100–250 THB per person. Bowls start at 69 THB (tom yum minced pork and lime), fish noodles run 89–150 THB, fish dumplings are 135 THB, and the mixed meatball platter is 190 THB. No booking needed and none possible — it's a walk-in-and-queue kind of place. There's a phone number to check if it's open: 0-2441-0655 or 093-346-6888. Hours are roughly daily 07:00–17:30, though Wongnai's latest listing shows it closed on Thursdays — calling ahead before you head out is the safer bet.

The shop sits on Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road, right at the mouth of Salaya Soi 17, near Mahidol University Salaya. There's no train station nearby (Salaya SRT station is several kilometres away), so driving or grabbing a taxi is the most convenient way in. The best time to go is morning through early afternoon, since the handmade fish balls sell well enough that they can run out by late afternoon. One thing to watch for: the shop also has a Bang Khun Non branch, but the one with the Bib Gourmand is Phutthamonthon Sai 4 — pin the right branch. Read the full review →

blocks.name: Plaew
blocks.descHtml:
The budget is very light — tom yum pork noodles run 60 baht a bowl, seafood tom yum with jumbo prawns runs 65 baht, and you can eat well for under a hundred baht a head, making it one of the cheapest MICHELIN listings (Bib Gourmand 2024–2026) on the list. No bookings taken since it's a small shophouse noodle shop — just walk in and sit down. There's a shop phone, 034-267-325, to check before you head out.

The thing people miss most often is the hours — the shop only sells in the afternoon, roughly 11:30–16:30 (some 2025 sources say it opens at noon), and it can sell out before closing. Weekends bring long queues since earning the MICHELIN badge, so aim to arrive right at opening, 11:30–12:00. The shop sits in the city of Nakhon Pathom, Soi 5, Mu 1, near Phra Pathom Chedi, close to the waterworks junction. There's no train line to it — you'll need to drive or take a van/train into Nakhon Pathom town. Watch out for confusion with the Bangkok branches (Huai Khwang, Thewet) — the MICHELIN-awarded shop is only the original Nakhon Pathom location. Read the full review →

faq.q: How many Michelin restaurants does Nakhon Pathom have in 2026?
faq.a: Three, and all of them are Bib Gourmand: Nai Ngieb fish-ball noodles, Plaew, and Krua Jay Sim. The province has no starred restaurants yet.

faq.q: If I only have one meal, where should I go?
faq.a: Go for Nai Ngieb, the town's signature fish-ball noodle shop. The handmade fish balls are springy and satisfying, bowls run 69 to 125 baht, and it's the dish locals are proudest of.

faq.q: Are Nakhon Pathom's Michelin restaurants expensive?
faq.a: Not at all. All three are street food and home-style spots. Plaew starts at 60 to 65 baht, Nai Ngieb at 69 to 125, and Krua Jay Sim around 150. You can hit all three for well under a thousand baht.

faq.q: Can I eat the whole list in one day?
faq.a: Easily. All three sit in Nakhon Pathom town, about an hour's drive from Bangkok. Pair Plaew and Nai Ngieb for lunch, then finish with Krua Jay Sim for dinner in a single trip.

faq.q: Beyond the 3 Bib Gourmand spots, are there other Michelin-listed places?
faq.a: Yes, a few Michelin Selected restaurants round out the list, including Somchai Go Tae in Bang Len, Banrimbung, Nai Ho Chicken Rice, and Loong Loy Pa Lan. They're good extras if you want to eat deeper.
